indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.5.1.1: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Know the need for and how to clean the teeth

skills.description: Explain why we clean our teeth
Name items used to clean teeth
Describe the correct method for cleaning teeth
Demonstrate the correct method of brushing teeth

misconceptions: Brushing hard is better than brushing gently.
You only need to brush in the morning.
Toothpaste alone is enough without a brush.

questions.stem: Why do we clean our teeth?
options: To keep them strong and white
questions.explanation: We clean our teeth to keep them strong and white.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think teeth cleaning is just for fun.

questions.stem: What do we use to brush our teeth?
hints: It is small enough for your mouth.
questions.explanation: A toothbrush is used to brush teeth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any brush can be used.

questions.stem: What do we put on the toothbrush to clean our teeth?
hints: It makes foam in your mouth.
questions.explanation: Toothpaste is used with a toothbrush to clean teeth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think soap is used on teeth.

questions.stem: How many times a day should you brush your teeth?
questions.explanation: You should brush your teeth at least twice a day.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think brushing once a week is enough.

questions.stem: Which direction should you move the toothbrush?
options: You don't need to move it
hints: Clean the top and bottom teeth.
questions.explanation: You should move the toothbrush in an upward and downward motion.
questions.misconception: Pupils may just scrub side to side.

questions.stem: What happens if you do not brush your teeth?
options: You can get cavities and bad breath
questions.explanation: If you do not brush your teeth, germs can cause cavities and bad breath.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize the consequences of poor oral hygiene.

questions.stem: Ama is going to brush her teeth. What does she need?
hints: She needs something to put on it.
questions.explanation: Ama needs a toothbrush and toothpaste to brush her teeth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may mix up items for different hygiene routines.

questions.stem: After brushing your teeth, what should you do?
hints: You need to spit out the foam.
questions.explanation: After brushing, you should rinse your mouth with water.

questions.stem: Which of these can be used to clean teeth if you don't have a toothbrush?
hints: It is a piece of wood.
People chew on it to clean.
questions.explanation: A chewing stick can be used to clean teeth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think only a plastic toothbrush works.

questions.stem: Why is brushing your teeth before bed important?
options: To remove food and germs from the day
To make your teeth fall out
questions.explanation: Brushing before bed removes food and germs, preventing them from staying on your teeth overnight.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think brushing in the morning is enough.

questions.stem: Name two things used for cleaning the teeth.
questions.explanation: A toothbrush and toothpaste are used to clean teeth.

questions.stem: What causes holes in the teeth?
options: Eating too much sweet food and not brushing
questions.explanation: Eating too much sweet food and not brushing can cause holes in teeth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think eating sweets is harmless.

questions.stem: Why should you brush gently and not too hard?
options: To make your teeth fall out
questions.explanation: You should brush gently to avoid hurting your gums.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think harder brushing is better.

questions.stem: Kofi says 'I don't need to brush my teeth because I chew gum.' Why is he wrong?
options: Chewing gum does not clean teeth like a toothbrush
Chewing gum is the same as brushing
hints: Chewing gum is not a brush.
questions.explanation: Chewing gum does not clean the teeth; you still need to brush with a toothbrush and toothpaste.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think chewing gum replaces brushing.

questions.stem: Adwoa sees her friend about to brush with soap. What should she tell her friend?
questions.explanation: Adwoa should tell her friend to use toothpaste instead of soap on her teeth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know the correct items for teeth.

questions.stem: Demonstrate to your teacher how to brush your teeth correctly.

criteria.description: Moves the brush up and down
Brushes for an appropriate time (or simulates)

questions.explanation: This tests the practical method of brushing teeth.

questions.stem: Draw the items you use for cleaning your teeth.
questions.explanation: This tests identification of dental hygiene items.

questions.stem: Write down two reasons why brushing your teeth is important.
questions.explanation: Brushing removes germs and prevents cavities.

questions.stem: Describe the steps for brushing your teeth.

criteria.description: Mentions putting toothpaste on the brush

hints: Start with the brush and paste.
questions.explanation: The steps are putting paste on the brush, brushing up and down, and rinsing.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher why you should not share your toothbrush.

criteria.description: States that it can spread germs
States that it is for personal use only

hints: Germs can pass from person to person.
questions.explanation: You should not share a toothbrush because it can spread germs.
